documents.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
documents.text: Retrieval-augmented generation combines document retrieval with language generation. The retriever supplies external knowledge as evidence before the language model creates an answer grounded in that context.

documents.title: Semantic Embeddings
documents.text: Embeddings represent text as dense numerical vectors. Semantic search compares vector similarity so that passages with related meanings can be retrieved even when their wording differs.

documents.title: Document Chunking
documents.text: Chunking divides long documents into smaller text segments. Overlap between adjacent chunks helps preserve context that would otherwise be lost at segment boundaries.

documents.title: Retrieval Reranking
documents.text: A reranker receives candidates from the initial retrieval stage and reorders them using a more precise relevance model. This improves the ordering of evidence sent to the generator.

documents.title: RAG Evaluation
documents.text: Retrieval quality can be measured with Recall at K and Mean Reciprocal Rank. Recall checks whether relevant evidence was found, while reciprocal rank rewards placing the first relevant result near the top.
